channel.title: AI Systems Architecture Handbook
channel.description: New and rewritten pages of the AI Systems Architecture Handbook.

item.title: The AI Component Model
item.description: What kind of component an LLM is, how tokens, context, and sampling shape its behavior, and why a measured quality rate is not the rate production delivers.

item.title: Capability vs. Reliability: Closing the Production Gap
item.description: Why benchmark and demo scores overstate delivered quality, how to measure pass^k and worst-slice rates, and how scope, checks, and abstention close it.

item.title: Anatomy of an LLM as a System Component: Tokens, Context, Sampling
item.description: How tokenization, a stateless bounded context window, and the sample-append-stop loop set the cost, latency, limits, and failure modes of every LLM call.

item.title: Deterministic vs. Probabilistic Systems: What Changes for Architecture
item.description: How contracts, retries, caching, testing, versioning, and auditing change when a component returns a sample from a distribution instead of a computed result.

item.title: Tool Call Idempotency, Retry, and Compensation
item.description: Why agents duplicate side effects through retries and re-planning, how to derive idempotency keys from intent, and how to compensate a half-executed plan.
